subject: c10-sst
note: Official 2026-27 course structure gives 20 marks each to History, Geography, Political Science and Economics, with map pointing included in History (2) and Geography (3). Making of a Global World is board-evaluated only for subtopics 1–1.3; Age of Industrialisation is periodic-assessment only; Lifelines of National Economy is map-pointing only in the board exam; Consumer Rights is project work; Globalisation and the Indian Economy is board-evaluated for What is Globalisation? and Factors that have enabled Globalisation, with the remaining listed project component assessed internally.

reference.label: History answer chain
reference.text: For a historical event, connect cause → event/process → important actors or groups → consequence. Use dates/names only when they strengthen the answer.

reference.label: History map work
reference.text: Practise the exact locations from the current syllabus. Learn the place name together with the event/resource it represents.

reference.label: Geography resource/crop questions
reference.text: For a resource or crop, revise distribution/location → conditions → major uses/production → relevant environmental or economic issue.

reference.label: Geography map work
reference.text: Separate map-pointing practice from theory revision; identify the location quickly and label it cleanly.

reference.label: Political Science
reference.text: For power-sharing and federalism, connect institutional arrangement → reason/need → example → democratic outcome. For parties and democracy, distinguish functions, challenges and outcomes.

reference.label: Economics development
reference.text: Do not equate development with income alone; use the indicators and limitations discussed in the chapter.

reference.label: Sectors of economy
reference.text: Compare primary, secondary and tertiary sectors by activity, employment/output and the issues highlighted in the chapter.

reference.label: Money and credit
reference.text: Keep formal and informal sources of credit separate and connect terms of credit with interest, collateral, documentation and risk.

reference.label: Globalisation
reference.text: Know the two board-assessed starting points clearly: what globalisation is and the factors that enabled it; keep project-only portions separate.

reference.label: Long answers
reference.text: Use a short introduction, several distinct points with examples/evidence, and a direct conclusion rather than one long paragraph.

mistakes: Do not treat Age of Industrialisation as a board-paper chapter; it is marked periodic-assessment only in the current course structure.
Do not prepare Consumer Rights as a board theory chapter; it is project work.
Lifelines of National Economy is board-assessed through map pointing only, so practise the map locations separately.
For source/case questions, use the information in the source together with the relevant chapter concept instead of writing an unrelated memorised answer.
In five-mark answers, use separate points and relevant examples; avoid repeating the same idea in different words.
order: Give all four disciplines balanced time because each carries 20 marks.
Build History and Geography together with map practice from the beginning.
Then revise Political Science and Economics through concept comparisons and short-answer practice.
Keep the restricted/project portions clearly separated in your notes so they are not confused with board-assessed content.
Finish with mixed case-study, long-answer and map practice.
